name: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd
title: ICICI Life Insurance Ltd - 540133 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Life insurer VNB up 24.9% to ₹5.71bn with margin 26.7%, but growth is protection-led while non-par and agency lag; management gave no guidance and called margin 'not a fixation'.

triggers.label: Retail protection up 60.4% YoY
triggers.quote: Our core focus area, retail protection, grew by 60.4% year-on-year in Q1-FY2027, driven by the GST exemption on protection products

triggers.label: Non-par sales subdued vs fixed-income alternatives
triggers.quote: The environment is such that pickup of non -par is quite subdued relative to previous periods.

triggers.label: No VNB or margin guidance given

red_flags.label: Non-linked APE down 9.5%; non-par not selling
red_flags.quote: in the current context, current environment, non-par is really not selling at this stage.

red_flags.label: Agency APE growth only 2%
red_flags.quote: Agency channel APE grew by 2% year -on-year in Q1 -FY2027 to ₹ 4.63 billion.

red_flags.label: Standard Chartered open-architecture uncertainty
red_flags.quote: I think they value the distribution partnership that they have with us and we continue to look at building it going forward.

evasions.quote: this is a question that's best answered by Standard Chartered
We've not disclosed that number, but we are very well within the cap.

summary.headline: ICICI Pru Life Q1 FY27: VNB up 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn at 26.7% margin, driven by retail protection growth of 60.4%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 VNB grew 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn, with VNB margin at 26.7%, up 200 bps from FY26's 24.7%. PAT rose 27.8% YoY to ₹3.86 bn. Growth was led by protection: sum assured up 31.8% to ₹4.90 trn and protection APE up 45.7%, while savings APE rose only 5.8% and non-linked APE fell about 9.5% as fixed deposits attracted customers. Management repeatedly stated there is no margin target and no formal guidance, and that absolute VNB growth is the focus.

segments.name: Retail protection
segments.commentary: Grew 60.4% YoY, third straight quarter above 40% after GST exemption; share of APE 10.5% vs 7.5% a year ago. Retail sum assured up 45.9% to ₹1.13 trn.

segments.name: Group protection (credit life + group term)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.8% YoY; MFI credit life recovered after a long slowdown, non-MFI momentum continued.

segments.name: Savings
segments.commentary: Savings APE ₹15.40 bn, up 5.8% YoY; savings share of mix fell to 72.1% from 78.1%. Linked APE up 6.4%; non-linked including annuity broadly flat at ₹4.94 bn; group funds up 42.2%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: APE up 2% YoY to ₹4.63 bn, improved from negative growth in prior quarters; channel shifting to higher sum assured and protection.

segments.name: Direct
segments.commentary: APE up 8.3% YoY to ₹2.86 bn; agency plus direct contributed 45.5% of retail APE.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 5.6% YoY, 27.4% of APE; management attributes this to partner-bank recalibration.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% YoY, 14.6% of APE; management cites a near 20% five-year CAGR and no single partner above 5%.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no VNB growth or margin guidance; it said margin is not a fixation and absolute VNB growth is the goal.
Second-half retail protection growth is expected to taper from the 60%+ level, as the base steepens; management said it would be 'very unlikely' to stay above 60% in H2.
The input tax credit drag continues for one more quarter (Q2) and then enters the base from Q3.
MFI credit life is expected to add to growth in H2 on a favourable base.
Non-par is expected to pick up only when fixed-deposit alternatives become less attractive; no timeline given.
No en-masse protection repricing is planned; repricing will be targeted by cohort as business as usual.
capex_capacity: Distribution: 2.44 lakh+ advisors, 52 bank partnerships covering 26,800+ bank branches, and 1,500+ non-bank partnerships.
Agency roadmap centres on micro-market-led branches and technology/analytics; management said FY27 agent additions would be similar to FY26's roughly 70,000.
Direct channel focus on online scaling and the NRI segment via GIFT City.
AI/ML is embedded across the customer journey, covering demand generation, automated underwriting, renewals, service and claims investigation (slide 32 of the investor presentation).
demand_pricing: Retail protection is growing on the GST exemption, which took effect after the GST reforms, plus pre-approved sum assured offers and digital income validation for onboarding.
Non-par savings is subdued because fixed deposits offer high sticker rates; management said the company is not staying away and keeps repricing.
Non-linked APE fell about 9.5% YoY, per a question from BNP Paribas; management attributed this to non-par weakness.
Annuity growth of about 33% YoY was led by regular-premium deferred annuity, not single premium; the par to non-par ratio in non-linked is about 2:1.
Persistency: 13th month 84.0% vs 84.5% at March; 25th month fell from 81% to 77% due to carry-through from last year's surrenders. Collections grew about 9%.
Management denied any en-masse protection price changes; the target protection buyer is around age 35.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin, and is the GST input tax credit drag still affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dhiren Salian said the margin was largely product mix; the non-availability of input tax credit continues for one more quarter (Q2) before entering the base from Q3. He did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-par not selling, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-income alternatives, mainly fixed deposits with high sticker rates, are more attractive to customers. Non-par is not being avoided and is repriced as conditions allow, but the pickup depends on those alternatives easing.

qa_highlights.question: Will Standard Chartered remain an open-architecture partner after Prudential's change in promoter status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Standard Chartered has been a 10-year partner, that both sides value it, and that ICICI Bank is the largest single channel at about 15% of business with no other distributor above 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How does expense management look, and what is the ITC drag in rupees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-premium is up on the input tax credit loss, partly offset by productivity and AI/ML gains. It did not quantify the ITC impact and said the schedules would show the GST component. It said EOM is well within the cap, without disclosing the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any VNB growth guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to give VNB growth guidance, including the 20-25% range an analyst proposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Prudential promoter-to-investor reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Prudential holds just under 22%. The board approved its request to reclassify as investor, and the company has submitted it to IRDAI, awaiting its response. Management said no sell-down is required under its reading of the rules.

risks_watch: Sharp H2 deceleration in retail protection, which management said will taper from 60%+ as the base steepens, could slow VNB growth.
Non-par savings and non-linked APE stay weak while fixed-deposit sticker rates remain high; the pickup timing is open.
Bank partner relationships, including Standard Chartered after Prudential's change in promoter status, and recalibration at partner banks (bancassurance +5.6%).
AUM outflows from surrenders and maturities (AUM ₹3.34 trn); 25th-month persistency fell to 77% from 81%.
Pending IRDAI decision on Prudential's promoter-to-investor reclassification, and the planned rename to ICICI Life Insurance Limited.
Possible NBFC insurance distribution rules from January, flagged by an analyst; management had no view.
summary.management_tone: Confident on protection and headline VNB growth, but evasive on forward numbers: management gave no VNB or margin guidance and repeatedly deflected on Standard Chartered, the Prudential reclassification and ITC quantification.
key_quotes: As a Company, we delivered a strong and resilient performance, with VNB growing by 24.9% year-on-year to ₹ 5.71 billion in Q1-FY2027, and VNB margins at 26.7%.
There is clearly no en-masse price change that we have done over the last 9 months nor are we expecting at this point.

adds.what: Agency micro-market-led branches (no count or capex given); FY27 agent additions similar to FY26's ~70,000

growth.why: No formal VNB or margin guidance; management said H2 retail protection growth will taper from 60%+ and is 'very unlikely' to stay above 60%, while growth is backed by GST exemption demand and an FY27 agent-addition plan similar to FY26's ~70,000, with no specific capacity or order numbers.
